# golden:  help-chat.w130
# surface: the /help command list in each session
# width:   130 columns
# palette: mono (two greys)
# cursor:  none
#
# Generated by go test -update-golden; do not edit by hand.
# The layout block is the render with ANSI stripped — read it for the
# columns. The ansi block is the same bytes with ESC written as ␛ — read
# it for the colour assignments. Trailing spaces are significant in both.

── layout ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
· a conversation
  commands
    /help          open the key list: every key this session answers, grouped as a keybindings.toml names them and spelled the way
                   they are bound now — type to filter by key or words, [esc] or [ctrl+]] closes it, and the draft is as you left
                   it. With words after it (/help keys), the whole sheet — the commands, what happens mid-turn, the keys and the
                   approval policy — is written to the transcript instead
    /clear         end this session and start another (also /new)
    /paste         attach the clipboard — a screenshot, or files copied in a file manager — to your next message; /paste <path>
                   attaches a file by name, /paste show <handle> opens a staged image or paste full-pane, /paste drop <handle>
                   takes one back out — the handle is the one a chip leads with, Image#1, and its name works too — and /paste
                   clear drops what is staged (ctrl+v). With a sentence half typed, reading mode (ctrl+o) keeps it and reaches the
                   strip of chips as its last row: ←→ picks a chip, enter opens it, x drops it, esc goes back to the sentence; a
                   click on a chip opens it too
    /copy [code]   copy the last response (or just its code blocks)
    /model [name]  switch the model (bare /model opens an interactive picker)
                   default [name]   show or persist the default model for new sessions
                   agents [name]    show or persist the model sub-agents run on ("inherit" follows the session model)
    /permissions   what runs without asking, and the permission mode that frames it (also /perms; was /mode)
                   [name]   bare opens a picker over the five modes:
                            manual asks about every consequential call
                            accept-edits applies the edits and asks for the rest
                            auto adds the allowlist and lets the classifier judge
                            read-only writes nothing — a write is refused, not asked
                            plan is read-only, ending on a plan you can approve here or carry into a fresh session
                   why      the latest auto-mode denial's reason
                   grants   what this session has stopped asking about
                   allow <commands|edits>   grant a whole category
                   revoke [commands|edits|hosts|agents]   take the grants back
    /reasoning     how much thinking the model does before it answers: off (the default), low, medium, high, xhigh or max — ctrl+t
                   cycles them
                   [level]           set it for this session (also /think)
                   default [level]   show or persist the level new sessions start on (provider.reasoning)
    /context       the window as a meter, by category, with the tools itemised
    /stats         the session's whole bill on one screen, as the rail's SPEND block reads it: the session total with the kinds of
                   request that make it up, each model's share with its own kinds and what the children on it cost, each child's
                   share by name, and each turn's cost as its close row states it. [enter] on a turn opens it on the turns screen.
                   What the context window is occupied by is /context. While attached to an agent, /stats is that agent's own. It
                   reads and changes nothing
    /readings      every reading the session has taken of its own run on one screen, newest first: the round, the verdict, the
                   whole reading with its reason and the instruction it was judged against, and whether it steered the turn and
                   whether that steer was taken back. Quiet readings are kept here too. It reads and changes nothing
    /turns         every turn the session has run on one screen, newest first: how it ended, its steps, tools, time and spend,
                   what it changed, its commit and its checks' verdict — the figures its close row drew, beside the close itself —
                   with the turn in flight on top. [enter] opens a turn's review where it changed files. A turn from an ended
                   sitting shows its files and says its figures were not kept. It reads and changes nothing
    /alerts        every alert the session has had on one screen, standing first and then superseded, newest first: the command,
                   its last outcome, its runs, the turn it first broke in and what answered it — a clean run or the quality gate
                   passing, with the turn. [enter] shows each run: its turn, how it ended, how long it took and the evidence id
                   its output was kept under where it was cut. It reads the rail's own alerts and changes nothing
    /step          open the in-flight step's card onto its calls, every call with its output body, bounded; run it again to close
                   (/ui verbosity high is the same thing for every card at once)
    /status        where this session is: what it is working on, what it has spent, and whether the last few turns are still on
                   the target you set it
    /sessions      the sessions running on this machine: the conversation each saves to, its checkout and branch, and whether it
                   is working
    /trust         let this checkout's own skills, agent profiles, wordings and quality suites load. A clone can carry
                   instructions, so nothing of a checkout's runs until you say so; "off" withdraws it and the next session starts
                   without them
    /ui            screen density, pane layout, monochrome and mouse: /ui verbosity <low|normal|high> · /ui mono <on|off> · /ui
                   mouse <on|off>
                   low draws each step's card as its header alone and leaves thinking out, normal draws the header, the sentence
                   and the evidence, high opens every card onto its calls; a card you opened or closed stays as you left it. The
                   mouse is on by default so the wheel scrolls the transcript, click-drag selects it, and clicks open rows, open
                   or close a card by its header, or answer keys; off hands selection back to the terminal, and ctrl+x flips it
                   and saves it
                   terminal   what this terminal answered when shhh asked what it can do: inline images, desktop notifications,
                              focus events, cell size
    /safety        the session's whole boundary on one screen (also /security): the mode and grants, where it may write, what
                   contains its commands, the hosts it reaches, what the checkout was let load, its servers, secrets and tools —
                   each section naming the command that changes it. It reads and changes nothing
    /skills        the skills this session loaded (SKILL.md directories), and why any did not
    /mcp           every place this session's tools came from on one screen, opened on the MCP servers: the built-in toolset, each
                   server, the language servers, the binaries found on PATH and the web tools, each up or not with the tools it
                   registered — and for one that is not up, what that costs and what would move it, in the words shhh mcp gives.
                   On a server the checkout declared, [a] trusts the checkout or withdraws that, after asking, as /trust does; it
                   takes effect in the next session. trust <name> and distrust <name> say where that answer is given
    /notes         the session's shared notebook — what the agents wrote for each other, and what a backlog run wrote up, listed
                   by author. Dropping is yours alone: drop <n> removes one, clear empties it
    /todo          the project's backlog: bare opens a picker · show|edit <slug> · add (reads this session into proposed items you
                   accept or drop) · add <text> · block <slug> [why] · open|done|drop <slug> · new <text> · groom <slug> (reads an
                   item against the tree and proposes the corrections) · run [slug|--next] works an item through its profile's run
                   · sprint · status · stop
    /compact       continue from a summary plus the most recent turns
    /rewind [n]    rewind to the end of turn [n], 0 being the start (bare /rewind picks interactively); the abandoned tail is kept
                   as a branch, and a card asks whether the files come back too
    /exit          quit (also /quit, /q)

· a coding session
  commands
    /help          open the key list: every key this session answers, grouped as a keybindings.toml names them and spelled the way
                   they are bound now — type to filter by key or words, [esc] or [ctrl+]] closes it, and the draft is as you left
                   it. With words after it (/help keys), the whole sheet — the commands, what happens mid-turn, the keys and the
                   approval policy — is written to the transcript instead

                   its output was kept under where it was cut. It reads the rail's own alerts and changes nothing
    /step          open the in-flight step's card onto its calls, every call with its output body, bounded; run it again to close
                   (/ui verbosity high is the same thing for every card at once)
    /steps         the session's own working list on one screen: every step it declared, the paths each said it would touch, which
                   it has marked done and the one it is on — and beside each, the calls the transcript titled for it, or not
                   started where there are none. It reads and changes nothing
    /status        where this session is: what it is working on, what it has spent, and whether the last few turns are still on
                   the target you set it
    /sessions      the sessions running on this machine: the conversation each saves to, its checkout and branch, and whether it

                   and saves it

                              focus events, cell size
    /sandbox       containment status and container sandboxes (doctor|scope|list|status|destroy <id>|prune)
    /safety        the session's whole boundary on one screen (also /security): the mode and grants, where it may write, what
                   contains its commands, the hosts it reaches, what the checkout was let load, its servers, secrets and tools —

                   by author. Dropping is yours alone: drop <n> removes one, clear empties it

                   accept or drop) · add <text> · block <slug> [why] · open|done|drop <slug> · new <text> · groom <slug> (reads an
                   item against the tree and proposes the corrections) · run [slug|--next] works an item through its profile's run
                   · sprint · status · stop
    /plan          the approved plan as a checklist on the steps screen — each step, the paths it named, its state and the calls
                   that carried it out — with anything that has departed from it · save [name] writes the last plan/response to
                   .shhh/plans/ · drop forgets an approved plan
    /diff [path]   show what this session changed, full screen, or one file's — read from the session's own changeset, so it works
                   outside a git repository
    /review [turn] review what a turn changed: file list, hunks and the turn's verdict (bare reviews the last turn that changed
                   anything). Also a turn's changed-files row, clicked or selected and opened with enter. It reads and changes
                   nothing; /undo takes a turn back
    /undo [turn]   put back what a turn changed, from the session's own records (not git). Asks first, names anything that changed
                   since, and is itself recorded as a turn
    /compact       continue from a summary plus the most recent turns
    /rewind [n]    rewind to the end of turn [n], 0 being the start (bare /rewind picks interactively); the abandoned tail is kept
                   as a branch, and a card asks whether the files come back too
    /exit          quit (also /quit, /q)

· a coding session
  ␛[38;5;244mcommands␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/help␛[m          ␛[38;5;244mopen the key list: every key this session answers, grouped as a keybindings.toml names them and spelled the way␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mthey are bound now — type to filter by key or words, [esc] or [ctrl+]] closes it, and the draft is as you left␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mit. With words after it (/help keys), the whole sheet — the commands, what happens mid-turn, the keys and the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mapproval policy — is written to the transcript instead␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/clear␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mend this session and start another (also /new)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/paste␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mattach the clipboard — a screenshot, or files copied in a file manager — to your next message; /paste <path>␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mattaches a file by name, /paste show <handle> opens a staged image or paste full-pane, /paste drop <handle>␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mtakes one back out — the handle is the one a chip leads with, Image#1, and its name works too — and /paste␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mclear drops what is staged (ctrl+v). With a sentence half typed, reading mode (ctrl+o) keeps it and reaches the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mstrip of chips as its last row: ←→ picks a chip, enter opens it, x drops it, esc goes back to the sentence; a␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mclick on a chip opens it too␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/copy [code]␛[m   ␛[38;5;244mcopy the last response (or just its code blocks)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/model [name]␛[m  ␛[38;5;244mswitch the model (bare /model opens an interactive picker)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mdefault [name]   show or persist the default model for new sessions␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244magents [name]    show or persist the model sub-agents run on ("inherit" follows the session model)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/permissions␛[m   ␛[38;5;244mwhat runs without asking, and the permission mode that frames it (also /perms; was /mode)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m[name]   bare opens a picker over the five modes:␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m         manual asks about every consequential call␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m         accept-edits applies the edits and asks for the rest␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m         auto adds the allowlist and lets the classifier judge␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m         read-only writes nothing — a write is refused, not asked␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m         plan is read-only, ending on a plan you can approve here or carry into a fresh session␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mwhy      the latest auto-mode denial's reason␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mgrants   what this session has stopped asking about␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mallow <commands|edits>   grant a whole category␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mrevoke [commands|edits|hosts|agents]   take the grants back␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/reasoning␛[m     ␛[38;5;244mhow much thinking the model does before it answers: off (the default), low, medium, high, xhigh or max — ctrl+t␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mcycles them␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m[level]           set it for this session (also /think)␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mdefault [level]   show or persist the level new sessions start on (provider.reasoning)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/context␛[m       ␛[38;5;244mthe window as a meter, by category, with the tools itemised␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/stats␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mthe session's whole bill on one screen, as the rail's SPEND block reads it: the session total with the kinds of␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mrequest that make it up, each model's share with its own kinds and what the children on it cost, each child's␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mshare by name, and each turn's cost as its close row states it. [enter] on a turn opens it on the turns screen.␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mWhat the context window is occupied by is /context. While attached to an agent, /stats is that agent's own. It␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mreads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/readings␛[m      ␛[38;5;244mevery reading the session has taken of its own run on one screen, newest first: the round, the verdict, the␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mwhole reading with its reason and the instruction it was judged against, and whether it steered the turn and␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mwhether that steer was taken back. Quiet readings are kept here too. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/turns␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mevery turn the session has run on one screen, newest first: how it ended, its steps, tools, time and spend,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mwhat it changed, its commit and its checks' verdict — the figures its close row drew, beside the close itself —␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mwith the turn in flight on top. [enter] opens a turn's review where it changed files. A turn from an ended␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244msitting shows its files and says its figures were not kept. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/alerts␛[m        ␛[38;5;244mevery alert the session has had on one screen, standing first and then superseded, newest first: the command,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mits last outcome, its runs, the turn it first broke in and what answered it — a clean run or the quality gate␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mpassing, with the turn. [enter] shows each run: its turn, how it ended, how long it took and the evidence id␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mits output was kept under where it was cut. It reads the rail's own alerts and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/step␛[m          ␛[38;5;244mopen the in-flight step's card onto its calls, every call with its output body, bounded; run it again to close␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m(/ui verbosity high is the same thing for every card at once)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/steps␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mthe session's own working list on one screen: every step it declared, the paths each said it would touch, which␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mit has marked done and the one it is on — and beside each, the calls the transcript titled for it, or not␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mstarted where there are none. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/status␛[m        ␛[38;5;244mwhere this session is: what it is working on, what it has spent, and whether the last few turns are still on␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mthe target you set it␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/sessions␛[m      ␛[38;5;244mthe sessions running on this machine: the conversation each saves to, its checkout and branch, and whether it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mis working␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/trust␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mlet this checkout's own skills, agent profiles, wordings and quality suites load. A clone can carry␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244minstructions, so nothing of a checkout's runs until you say so; "off" withdraws it and the next session starts␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mwithout them␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/ui␛[m            ␛[38;5;244mscreen density, pane layout, monochrome and mouse: /ui verbosity <low|normal|high> · /ui mono <on|off> · /ui␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mmouse <on|off>␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mlow draws each step's card as its header alone and leaves thinking out, normal draws the header, the sentence␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mand the evidence, high opens every card onto its calls; a card you opened or closed stays as you left it. The␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mmouse is on by default so the wheel scrolls the transcript, click-drag selects it, and clicks open rows, open␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mor close a card by its header, or answer keys; off hands selection back to the terminal, and ctrl+x flips it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mand saves it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mterminal   what this terminal answered when shhh asked what it can do: inline images, desktop notifications,␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m           focus events, cell size␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/sandbox␛[m       ␛[38;5;244mcontainment status and container sandboxes (doctor|scope|list|status|destroy <id>|prune)␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/safety␛[m        ␛[38;5;244mthe session's whole boundary on one screen (also /security): the mode and grants, where it may write, what␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mcontains its commands, the hosts it reaches, what the checkout was let load, its servers, secrets and tools —␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244meach section naming the command that changes it. It reads and changes nothing␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/skills␛[m        ␛[38;5;244mthe skills this session loaded (SKILL.md directories), and why any did not␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/mcp␛[m           ␛[38;5;244mevery place this session's tools came from on one screen, opened on the MCP servers: the built-in toolset, each␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mserver, the language servers, the binaries found on PATH and the web tools, each up or not with the tools it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mregistered — and for one that is not up, what that costs and what would move it, in the words shhh mcp gives.␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mOn a server the checkout declared, [a] trusts the checkout or withdraws that, after asking, as /trust does; it␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mtakes effect in the next session. trust <name> and distrust <name> say where that answer is given␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/notes␛[m         ␛[38;5;244mthe session's shared notebook — what the agents wrote for each other, and what a backlog run wrote up, listed␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mby author. Dropping is yours alone: drop <n> removes one, clear empties it␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/todo␛[m          ␛[38;5;244mthe project's backlog: bare opens a picker · show|edit <slug> · add (reads this session into proposed items you␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244maccept or drop) · add <text> · block <slug> [why] · open|done|drop <slug> · new <text> · groom <slug> (reads an␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mitem against the tree and proposes the corrections) · run [slug|--next] works an item through its profile's run␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m· sprint · status · stop␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/plan␛[m          ␛[38;5;244mthe approved plan as a checklist on the steps screen — each step, the paths it named, its state and the calls␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mthat carried it out — with anything that has departed from it · save [name] writes the last plan/response to␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244m.shhh/plans/ · drop forgets an approved plan␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/diff [path]␛[m   ␛[38;5;244mshow what this session changed, full screen, or one file's — read from the session's own changeset, so it works␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244moutside a git repository␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/review [turn]␛[m ␛[38;5;244mreview what a turn changed: file list, hunks and the turn's verdict (bare reviews the last turn that changed␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244manything). Also a turn's changed-files row, clicked or selected and opened with enter. It reads and changes␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mnothing; /undo takes a turn back␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/undo [turn]␛[m   ␛[38;5;244mput back what a turn changed, from the session's own records (not git). Asks first, names anything that changed␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244msince, and is itself recorded as a turn␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/compact␛[m       ␛[38;5;244mcontinue from a summary plus the most recent turns␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/rewind [n]␛[m    ␛[38;5;244mrewind to the end of turn [n], 0 being the start (bare /rewind picks interactively); the abandoned tail is kept␛[m
                   ␛[38;5;244mas a branch, and a card asks whether the files come back too␛[m
    ␛[38;5;254m/exit␛[m          ␛[38;5;244mquit (also /quit, /q)␛[m
